text:
margot: Heads-up — prod spike hit our SSE clients earlier. Multiple apps saw truncated JSON chunks and fast consumers dropping fragments. Repro when QPS > 120/s. Any quick ideas before I open a long investigation? :grimacing:

kai: ouch. do we have logs showing split utf8 boundaries or just partial object fragments?

margot: logs show `Partial JSON at end of frame` a lot, then a flurry of `Unexpected end of input` in the client. Example payload: `{"id":123, "text":"...emoji \ud83d...` gets cut mid-emoji.

sam: that sounds like chunk boundary splitting multibyte chars + naive JSON.parse. Are we using a streaming decoder or just buffer.concat + JSON.parse?

margot: Node client is doing incremental buffer concat then try-parse loop. We suspected `TextDecoder` streaming might help but didn't get time to switch.

lee: short checklist: 1) ensure server sends `

` delimiter between events or NDJSON; 2) on client use `TextDecoder` with `stream: true` and accumulate strings (not raw bytes) before JSON.parse; 3) keep a small bounded queue and apply backpressure to readers.

sam: Agree. Also add a lightweight incremental parser fallback: try parse, if fails, check last few bytes for high-bit sequences and wait for next chunk. For Node: use `new TextDecoder().decode(chunk, { stream: true })` then append to scalar string.

kai: Another operational mitigation: throttle the read loop on the SSE fetch to give downstream code time to process. e.g. insert a micro-delay when queue length > N. Prevents memory blowups.

margot: Good. Is there a quick patch we can push to the JS SDK today so downstream apps get a safer default?

sam: I can PR a tiny change: switch our SSE reader to stream-decoder + buffered-string reassembly + max-buffer-size with emit-error. Pseudocode in PR description. Will link in a minute.

sam: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/client-sdk/pull/421 — adds `TextDecoder({ fatal: false })` streaming path, `maxBufferedChars: 64_000`, and a `pause()` hook consumers can call.

lee: will that handle emoji splits? TextDecoder with stream true should, yea. Also add a heartbeat/reconnect backoff so we don't hammer reconnects on partial-json errors.

kai: One more: log a short hex prefix of the raw bytes when parse fails so we can tell whether split occurred in a multibyte sequence vs truncated object vs protocol framing issue. Keep logs capped to e.g. 64 bytes.

margot: Sounds like a plan. For immediate prod mitigation: enable connection-level rate-limit and roll the client patch as an emergency release. Sam can you also add a small e2e test that simulates chunk splits (multibyte inside) so it won't regress?

sam: yep — adding tests to `tests/streaming-split.test.js` that feed half emoji then remainder.

deploy-bot: CI passed for PR #421 — integration tests green. Deploy to canary? :rocket:

lee: canary first: route 2% traffic, watch `sse.partial_json_rate` and `client.retry_rate`. Set alert if partial_json_rate > 0.5% per minute.

margot: I'll open the canary rollout and ping product owners. Also scheduling a follow-up async doc with the recommended parsing pattern and small code snippets for Rust/Go/Swift.

kai: tiny nit — for server teams, please try to follow NDJSON or event framing (
 delimiter) guarantees. It makes client robustness much easier.

margot: thanks everyone. If anyone sees anything odd during canary ping me here. We'll keep this thread for quick triage. :thumbsup:
